current.text: Trae Young re-signed with Washington on a 4 year, 213 million deal.
He is the Wizards' starting point guard and offensive engine. He handles the ball the most, and his role is secure.
Last season's numbers came in only about 25 to 26 minutes a game because of injuries, so they understate him.
Experts expect about 33 to 35 minutes a night, clearly more than last season, but doubt he gets back to 36.
He shares usage with Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa. Experts project about 29% usage, well below his career peak, which caps his scoring.
He should finish clearly better than last season's rank in the 80s thanks to more minutes.

Experts call him a bust at his Yahoo rank of 18 and ESPN rank of 14. They put him outside the top 24 for categories and see him as fair around pick 26 at best, mainly for teams that badly need assists.
His range is wide: best case about 13th, worst case about 78th.
His improved efficiency from last season (69% at the rim, 62 true shooting) is not expected to hold.
His FT% should return to about 86%, and his rebounds could rise to about three with more minutes.
Experts are not worried about his health. They warn against overreacting to one injury year.
Washington is trying to compete for the play-in at about 40 wins, so late-season rest and minutes cuts are not expected.
Head coach Brian Keefe is under the most pressure to win games this season.

durable.text: He is a multiple-time All-Star who has consistently put up 20 points and 10 assists.
He is one of the best passers in the NBA, a top five passer.
He is one of the worst defenders in the NBA.
Assists are a league outlier. FG% on real volume and turnovers are his weak categories.
He is closer to a 35% three-point shooter than a 38% one. Rebounds, steals and blocks are low.
In categories, his downsides outweigh his very good assists.
He is not injury prone. Last season was his only real missed time, and much of it was overstated.

note: He went for 44 USD in our league last season, and Yahoo values him at 38 USD. ESPN values him at only 11 USD, and the experts say he is a bust at rank 18, so he is only worth a price that fits around pick 26. His 10.4 projected assists are elite, but his 42% FG% and 4.2 turnovers hurt, so he fits punt FG% and punt TO builds that need assists. Early in the season, check that he reaches 33 or more minutes and see how much usage he keeps next to Davis and Dybantsa.
